lines.1: After beating up delinquents from my own school and finding people keeping their distance, I stopped acting wild.
lines.2: I couldn't stand being hated by classmates I'd always gotten along with.
lines.3: I wasn't strong enough to say something like Subaru: 'As long as I have you guys, that's enough.'
lines.4: Konoe's injuries caused a stir for a while, but since she acted exactly as usual, the rumors died down.
lines.5: Some of the delinquents transferred schools, and the whole incident eventually became vague history.
lines.6: I wanted to protect that newly stable atmosphere--
lines.7: But the cultural festival shattered it completely.
lines.8: Our class started fighting over what play to perform.
lines.9: 「Come on! This is a memory of middle school for all of us. Let's work hard and do it right!」
lines.10: Konoe argued passionately as class representative.
lines.11: But everyone around her was cold.
lines.12: Their reason was simple: it sounded like too much work.
lines.13: To classmates who were lazy and unwilling to unite, Konoe was obviously annoying.
lines.14: Our homeroom teacher became furious at the class for refusing to cooperate.
lines.15: Even that anger just felt annoying to them.
lines.16: Whose fault was it that the teacher had gotten this mad?
lines.17: Obviously, they decided it was Konoe's--the one person actually trying.
lines.18: The next day, at the shoe lockers.
lines.21: Konoe's shoes were covered in insults.
lines.23: Thinking about it, our class hadn't had a bullying target before.
lines.24: Subaru stood apart from everyone, but that was because people feared him.
lines.25: Nobody would choose him as a victim.
lines.28: A group sometimes seeks a sacrifice.
lines.31: They didn't resort to open violence. They hid things, broke things, and worked in secret.
lines.32: The sheer pettiness of the bullying pissed me off.
lines.33: If they had a complaint, they should say it to her face.
lines.34: But no matter what they did, Konoe refused to break.
lines.35: On the way home from cram school, at our usual place--
lines.36: Konoe looked up at the moon and talked.
lines.38: 「My mother is an actress. I guess I got it from her.」
lines.40: 「No. She's a stage actress, so it's a little different.」
lines.41: 「That's why I'm interested in this stuff.」
lines.42: 「So that's why you're so fired up.」
lines.43: 「Yeah... And I want this to be a good memory.」
lines.46: This time, I wanted to protect her.
lines.47: To make up for letting her get hurt before.
lines.48: But at homeroom the next day, she kept spinning her wheels.
lines.49: 「At this rate, when it's our turn for the play, the teacher will just read an apology and that'll be the end of it!」
lines.52: They had decided their refusal to cooperate was Konoe's fault for being annoying.
lines.53: They would rather do nothing than take orders from her.
lines.54: A strange solidarity had formed around that idea.
lines.56: I couldn't take it anymore and stood up.
lines.57: 「She's right. We're getting nowhere like this.」
lines.58: 「Come on, everyone. Why don't we actually try?」
lines.59: 「There's still something we can do, even now!」
lines.60: I did my best to support Konoe.
lines.64: 'He's kind of a try-hard, isn't he?'
lines.65: 'How about this week's class goal: Don't try so hard?'
lines.67: And the harassment of Konoe seemed to be escalating too.
lines.71: Apparently I was the class try-hard now.
lines.72: Of all the stupid nicknames to get.
lines.74: If I kept pushing, I'd become isolated too.
lines.76: So I decided to talk to Konoe.
lines.77: I asked her to stay in the classroom until evening so we could be alone.
lines.78: 「I want to talk to you, just the two of us.」
lines.79: For some reason, Konoe blushed bright red and nodded.
